SEARCH
Package engine

Class FFmpegAudioEngine

java.lang.Object
engine.FFmpegAudioEngine
All Implemented Interfaces:
FormatAudioEngine, AutoCloseable
public class FFmpegAudioEngine extends Object implements FormatAudioEngine
FFmpeg-based audio playback engine with advanced audio processing capabilities. This class provides a high-performance audio playback engine that leverages FFmpeg for decoding multiple audio formats (MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, etc.) and supports playback control features such as play, pause, resume, stop, seeking, and volume adjustment.

Key Features:

  • Multi-format audio decoding using FFmpeg
  • Real-time audio processing with gain control
  • Playback control: play, pause, resume, stop
  • Precision seeking within audio files
  • Thread-safe operations with ReentrantLock
  • Low-latency audio output (32KB buffer)
  • 16-bit PCM stereo output at 44.1kHz

Audio Processing Pipeline: 

 FFmpeg Decoder (float 32-bit)
     ↓
 GainProcessor (volume control)
     ↓
 AudioUtils.floatsToBytes (16-bit PCM conversion)
     ↓
 SourceDataLine (system audio output)

Thread Safety: The engine uses a ReentrantLock to protect critical sections where the decoder is accessed. The playback runs on a separate high-priority thread (AudioPlaybackThread).

Usage Example: 


 GainProcessor gainProcessor = new GainProcessor();
 FFmpegAudioEngine engine = new FFmpegAudioEngine(gainProcessor, "audio.mp3");

 try {
     engine.play();
     Thread.sleep(5000); // Play for 5 seconds
     engine.pause();
     Thread.sleep(2000);
     engine.resume();
     engine.seek(30.0); // Seek to 30 seconds
     engine.setVolume(0.8f); // 80% volume
 } finally {
     engine.close();
 }

  • Method Details

    • play

      public void play() throws AudioException
      Starts audio playback from the beginning of the file.

      This method performs the following operations:

      • Stops any existing playback
      • Creates and opens a new FFmpeg decoder
      • Initializes the audio output line (SourceDataLine)
      • Starts a high-priority playback thread

      The playback runs asynchronously on a separate thread. Audio data is continuously decoded, processed for gain, converted to PCM bytes, and written to the system audio output.

      Specified by:
      play in interface FormatAudioEngine
      Throws:
      AudioFileException - if the audio file cannot be opened or accessed
      AudioDecodingException - if audio decoding cannot be initialized
      AudioPlaybackException - if the playback system fails to initialize
      AudioException - for other audio-related errors
      See Also:
      • pause()
      • resume()
      • stop()

    • pause

      public void pause()
      Pauses the current audio playback.

      The audio output line is stopped, but the playback position is maintained. Call resume() to continue playback from the pause point.

      This method has no effect if playback is not active or already paused.

      Specified by:
      pause in interface FormatAudioEngine
      See Also:
      • resume()
      • stop()

    • resume

      public void resume()
      Resumes audio playback from the current pause point.

      This method restarts the audio output line to continue playing from where playback was paused.

      This method has no effect if playback is not active or not paused.

      Specified by:
      resume in interface FormatAudioEngine
      See Also:
      • pause()
      • play()

    • stop

      public void stop() throws AudioProcessingException
      Stops the current audio playback completely.

      This method performs the following operations:

      • Sets gain to 0 to silence audio
      • Sleeps for 50ms to allow sound to fade
      • Calls internalStop() to release resources

      The playback state is reset and the audio position is reset to the beginning. After calling this method, call play() to start playback again from the beginning.

      Specified by:
      stop in interface FormatAudioEngine
      Throws:
      AudioProcessingException
      See Also:
      • pause()
      • play()

    • seek

      public void seek(double seconds) throws AudioSeekException
      Seeks to a specific position in the audio file.

      This method performs the following operations:

      • Temporarily pauses playback
      • Flushes the output buffer
      • Calls seek on the decoder (thread-safe with lock)
      • Clears the float buffer to prevent audio artifacts
      • Resumes playback from the new position
      Specified by:
      seek in interface FormatAudioEngine
      Parameters:
      seconds - the seek position in seconds from the start of the file
      Throws:
      AudioSeekException - if seek fails or decoder is not initialized
      See Also:
      • getDuration()
      • FFmpegAudioDecoder.seek(double)

    • close

      public void close() throws AudioResourceException
      Closes the audio engine and releases all resources.

      This method performs the following cleanup operations:

      • Stops audio playback via internalStop()
      • Interrupts the playback thread
      • Waits up to 500ms for the playback thread to terminate

      After calling this method, the engine should not be used. A new instance should be created to play another audio file.

      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
      Specified by:
      close in interface FormatAudioEngine
      Throws:
      AudioResourceException - if an error occurs during resource cleanup
      See Also:
      • play()
      • stop()
